summary: Create, edit, archive and delete a holding: name, native unit which doubles as its rate symbol, one dimension value per axis, and a note, all encrypted client-side. Archiving records the holding's zero on the day it is made, refreshing that day's prices like any recording, and a permanent delete cascades server-side.

payloadShape.value: { name, unit, dims, note, archivedAt, createdAt }

unitIsTheRateSymbol.value: unit is what the account is measured in and is also its rate symbol: either a row of the operator's table or free text for a holding with no market price. There is no separate rate-symbol field, because two fields could disagree and a gram-versus-troy-ounce mismatch is silent

unitNamesTheBaseAssetOnly.value: the quote currency is the user's main currency and travels as a separate quote parameter, so a pair like USDCHF is never a unit

formattingFollowsSettings.value: formatting follows the reader's settings, not the unit, so the account record carries no kind

dimsShape.value: a map from dimension id to value id, both opaque ids from the profile's dimension config, carrying no display text. A JSON object cannot carry the same key twice, so a second value for one dimension is unrepresentable

dimensionIdFormat.value: 8 characters of [a-z0-9], generated client-side at creation. Never a label-derived key, which could collide with a string already in user data

missingDimsEntry.value: a real state, rendered as Unassigned, never an error and never hidden. Nothing is backfilled at dimension-creation time. A value id naming no configured value, because the value or its dimension was archived, also renders as Unassigned, and the entry stays on the account untouched

noServerSideDimensionEntity.value: a server-side list would leak the classification graph. Everything the UI shows is derived client-side from the decrypted profile and accounts

archivedAt.value: null for an active account, otherwise the ISO date the account was archived

deleteIsAUserChoice.value: an account with snapshots presents two explicit options, archive preselected as the default, and permanent delete. An account with no snapshots skips the dialog and is deleted outright, and reaches the archive dialog only from the holding's own Archive action

archiveDate.value: D is the day the archive is made. The dialog shows it and does not offer a choice

archiveMeansZero.value: archiving writes the holding's zero at D. The dialog has no value field and there is no way to archive without the zero. The holding leaves active lists and the current total, takes no new snapshots, every snapshot before D stays as it was, and it is reversible

archiveZeroShape.value: an ordinary snapshot { "date": D, "value": "0", "note": null } with the holding's plaintext account_id. Nothing in it marks it as the archive's. The archive's zero is the zero-valued snapshot at a holding's archivedAt while archivedAt is set, so the record shape, export and import learn nothing new

archiveIsARecording.value: the zero is a recording: it joins the recording at D or starts one, and refreshes D's prices like any recorded quantity

archiveWriteOrder.value: 1 the zero at D, by what D holds for this holding. 2 D's price entries, ensured over the units of the active holdings as they stand, this holding still among them. 3 the account record with archivedAt D at version + 1. The zero goes before the prices because prices written with the quantity then failing would move every holding in those units for a figure that is not there. The prices go before the flag because the refresh covers active holdings only, so a flag set first would drop this holding's unit out of the set and leave D unpriced for every other holding in it. The flag goes last because each earlier step alone leaves a true state, and a flag written first with the zero failing would leave an archived holding stepping off its last figure and unable to take the snapshot that would repair it

archiveReload.value: before its first create the archive runs the pre-create reload of type=snapshot and type=rate, once, and decides every step from what it returned. An archive that creates nothing runs no reload. It is refused only when the reload finds this holding's own slot at D taken: other holdings' records at D are the recording the zero joins, and a rate slot taken since is one the refresh leaves alone. A refused archive writes nothing and the dialog reopens on what D now holds

archiveZeroByWhatDHolds.value: nothing: a create at a fresh UUIDv4 and version 1. A non-zero figure: the dialog states before its confirm that the zero replaces it, named in the holding's unit, and on confirm the record is updated in place with the same record_id, version + 1, a fresh nonce, value "0" and note kept, with no replace prompt. A zero in any canonical form ("0", "0.00"): nothing is written and no replacement is stated, which is the retry path after a failed flag write, and a stored "0.00" keeps its digits

archivePrices.value: ensured means created only where D has no entry for a symbol: a date that already holds a recording keeps every rate it holds, and a retry rewrites none it already wrote. A date whose prices are complete issues no request to /api/rates, and a unit the proxy returns no proposal for gets no entry. The dialog has no rate lines and asks for no price

archiveNoSnapshots.value: a holding with no snapshots archives the same way, so the zero is its only figure at version 1. It appears on no chart date, and unarchived it reads zero, not not yet valued. The zero is a recorded figure, so from then on its unit is fixed, archived or not

archiveFailures.value: the zero did not save: no price and no account write, the holding is untouched and the dialog stays open saying so. Conflict on the replacement: surfaced, never retried, the dialog reloads that record and states the replacement again with the figure now stored. A price did not save: the archive still goes through, because a price write cannot fail a quantity write, the message names the units whose prices were not written, and nothing is rolled back. The flag did not save: the zero and the prices written stay at D, the holding stays active and counts at zero, both halves are stated and the archive is offered again, and the retry finds the zero, writes only the prices still missing, then the flag. The archive refused after the reload: nothing written, the dialog reopens on what D now holds

archiveReplacementLinePlacement.value: at phone width the line naming a replaced figure is on screen together with the confirm button, because the confirm consents to it

archiveChartReach.value: the holding counts on chart dates before D and on none from D on. Archiving deletes no snapshot. The zero and any price entries the refresh adds at D each move what a new last entry moves, the dates after the previous entry in their own series, and nothing before it. The band interpolates into the zero, so the days between can change like they do for any new last figure. D carries an archive annotation

whileArchived.value: no new snapshot at any date. The archive's zero is read-only: it cannot be edited, cleared or deleted, from the holding's page or from the recording for D. An entry's date moves only to a date before D. Every other snapshot stays editable and deletable, including a non-zero figure at D, which becomes the archive's zero when edited to zero. Deleting the recording at D keeps the zero: every other record at D goes, the date stays a recording holding the zero, and the confirmation says so. A purge still takes the zero with every other snapshot

archivedEntryDateRefusal.value: an archived holding's entry takes the day before the archive date as the date field's upper limit and the archive as its reason. The grid disables every day from D on. A typed date on or after D is refused on the date field's own message line, a date after today included, with the archive's reason and never the future-date one, because D is never later than today. Copy: 'Archived on 12 March 2026. Enter an earlier date.', the date computed in the Settings order and always with its year. From the moment the dialog opens the message line carries the hint 'Archived on 12 March 2026.' in ink-secondary, and an entry on a holding that is not archived has no hint, its line staying reserved. The refusal clears as soon as a date before D is entered, before Save, and Save with a refused date issues no PUT

whileArchivedIsClientEnforced.value: the server sees neither a date nor archivedAt. A session whose model predates the archive can still write a figure for the holding at D or later, and no such figure reaches a total because the chart counts an archived holding on no date from D on

unarchive.value: clears archivedAt at version + 1 and writes nothing else, with no dialog. The zero stays a figure like any other: the holding rejoins active lists and the current total at zero until a new figure is recorded, and the zero becomes editable. Its unit rejoins the set the next recording refreshes

archivedWithoutAZero.value: a holding archived on D whose figure at D is not zero, or which has none, keeps its history as it is and gains no snapshot on unlock, on any read or on any write elsewhere. The chart draws its step at D. Unarchiving it and archiving it again writes the zero at the new D

purge.value: DELETE /api/accounts/<account_id>?mode=purge removes the account record and cascades to every snapshot carrying that account_id, server-side and atomically. It deletes no price entry, because a price belongs to a symbol and the symbol is inside the ciphertext. Requires typing the account name to confirm, and the dialog states plainly that past net-worth figures will change

disabledConfirmLook.value: the permanent-delete confirm is disabled until the typed name matches, in the one disabled look every primary, secondary and destructive button shares: petrol-200 fill and border, label ink-secondary at 5.24:1, no hover change, cursor default, no opacity, and no critical red, so the confirm turns red only once it can act

purgeComparesEpoch.value: the purge compares the vault epoch after BEGIN IMMEDIATE, because an import keeps record ids and a purge from a page holding the replaced DEK would otherwise delete a restored holding. A replaced epoch answers Conflict {"refused":"vault-replaced"} and leaves the holding and every one of its snapshots in place

cascadeReach.value: no other record type carries an account link, so nothing else can be swept up by the cascade

namesAreNotUnique.value: two accounts may share a name. The record_id is identity

unitIsFrozenOnceRecorded.value: changing the unit of an account that already has snapshots is blocked, because the existing quantities are counted in the old unit and a new unit would price the whole history off a different symbol's series. The archive's zero counts, so a holding archived and unarchived with no other value keeps its unit locked. Client-enforced by construction, since unit lives inside the ciphertext. Renaming, re-classifying and editing the note are always allowed

everyWriteReEncrypts.value: every write re-encrypts the whole record with a fresh nonce and increments version

renderingRule.value: decrypted names, notes and dimension labels are rendered with x-text or textContent only, never x-html

staleVersionOnEdit.condition: a concurrent edit from a second tab. The UI reloads and asks the user to redo the edit. The body has no refused member (spec/features/manage-accounts.md#edge-cases, spec/architecture.md#status-codes)

purgeWithReplacedEpoch.condition: a purge whose X-Solvent-Vault is the epoch from before an import. The body is {"refused":"vault-replaced"}, nothing is deleted, and the page closes the vault instead of reloading (spec/features/manage-accounts.md#acceptance-criteria)

purgeOnAnotherUsersAccount.condition: Not Found, never Forbidden, and nothing is deleted (spec/features/manage-accounts.md#acceptance-criteria)

focus: the disabled permanent-delete confirm must be asserted on computed style, disabled and then enabled: petrol-200 fill and border, ink-secondary label, opacity 1, no red while disabled, red once the name matches. A button dimmed with opacity or left red keeps the label under 4.5:1 or shows an action that cannot act, and passes a test of the disabled attribute alone

the unit-change block must be asserted against the UI refusing it, not against an API call being rejected. The server cannot see the unit, so a test written against the endpoint asserts a control that does not exist and would pass against a client that allows the change
purge must be shown to delete no rate record, asserted by count before and after, because the failure is silent and only shows up later as a repriced history
purge atomicity needs a fault injected mid-delete, with neither the account record nor its snapshots partially gone afterwards

a purge naming a restored holding with the pre-import epoch must answer vault-replaced and leave the holding and every snapshot in place, compared row for row. Import keeps record ids, so the id exists in the restored vault and a purge that only checks the id deletes it

an edit's Conflict on a stale version must stay distinguishable from vault-replaced by the refused member, and only the first runs the reload-and-redo. A form that reloads on both works against a vault that no longer exists

the archive write order must be asserted on the wire with each write stubbed to fail in turn: the zero, then the prices, then the flag. A flag written first passes every happy-path test and archives a holding stepping off its last figure with no way to repair it

after archiving a holding with no snapshots and unarchiving it, changing its unit must be refused at the UI. The zero is a recorded figure, and a lock keyed on the person having typed a value passes every other unit test

the archive's price step must be asserted both ways by count: on a D holding no prices it writes one entry per needed unit, this holding's unit included, and on a D whose prices are complete it issues no request and rewrites none byte for byte. Writing nothing passes the second and fails the first, and writing every time passes the first and rewrites a recording's stored prices

a price write that fails must not stop the archive, and a flag that fails must leave the holding active with the zero and the prices written, the retry writing only what is missing. A client that rolls back or aborts on a price failure passes every happy path

the refresh must run while the holding is still active, so its own unit is priced at D: assert the unit has an entry at D after archiving a holding that is the last one measured in it. A flag written before the prices drops that unit and leaves D unpriced for the others

the archive's reload must cover both types, run once, and run not at all when the archive creates nothing, asserted as a request count and position. Both halves are invisible to an end-state assertion

archiving onto a D holding a non-zero figure must name that figure before the confirm, show no replace prompt, and leave exactly one snapshot for that (holding, D) with the same record_id, version + 1, a different nonce, value "0" and the note unchanged. Half of this is about a prompt not appearing, which no happy-path test catches

archiving onto a D holding "0.00" must write no snapshot and leave that record byte-identical, and the retry after a failed flag must issue no snapshot write and exactly one account PUT. An implementation that always writes "0" passes the first archive and fails both

the archive refusal must be asserted in both directions: refused when the second session recorded this holding at D, not refused when it recorded only other holdings at D. A reload that refuses on any record at D passes the first and breaks every archive on a day with a sitting
the archive dialog must be shown to offer no value field and no way to archive without the zero. Absence is the assertion, and a screenshot of one happy path does not make it

the read-only zero must be asserted against the controls on every surface, the holding's row actions, the update row for D and the snapshot form's date picker, not against an API call. The server cannot see the date or archivedAt, so an endpoint test asserts a rule that does not exist there

an archived holding's entry typed with D, with a date between D and today and with a date after today must each be refused with the archive's reason on the date field's own line, never the future-date wording, with aria-invalid set and no PUT issued. A date limited only by today passes the future case and lets the others save, and a test of the grid alone misses typed dates
deleting the recording at D must leave the zero byte-identical with the date still opening, and unarchiving must write only the account record. Both are about a write that must not happen

a holding archived without a zero at D must gain no snapshot on unlock, on any read or on any write elsewhere, asserted by comparing every snapshot record before and after. A migration that tidies it is invisible in the UI

'no account record contains a rate symbol distinct from its unit' is asserted against the record shape itself, so that the 31x mismatch has nowhere to live. A value-level check would pass a schema that still admits the field
renaming a dimension label must leave every account record byte-identical, compared row by row rather than by counting writes
an account whose dims names an archived value must render as Unassigned with no account record written in either direction, restore included
the XSS assertion has to cover every place a decrypted string reaches, the list, the chart legend and every tooltip, not just the account form, because the rendering path differs between them
